questions.prompt:
Part (a): Verify that \(B=S^{-1}AS\) with \(A=\operatorname{diag}(14,16)\) and \(S=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) equals \(\operatorname{diag}(16,14)\).
Part (b): Prove that commuting diagonalizable matrices with simple spectrum have a common eigenbasis.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Since \(S^{-1}=S\), direct multiplication gives
\[SAS=\begin{pmatrix}16&0\\0&14\end{pmatrix}.\]
Final answer: \(B=\operatorname{diag}(16,14)\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
If \(A\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v\), then \(A(B\mathbf v)=B(A\mathbf v)=\lambda B\mathbf v\), so \(B\mathbf v\) lies in the one-dimensional \(\lambda\)-eigenspace. Hence \(B\mathbf v=\mu\mathbf v\). Apply this to the eigenbasis of \(A\).
Final answer: The eigenbasis of \(A\) is also an eigenbasis of \(B\).

Part (a): Calculate the commutator of \(A=\operatorname{diag}(15,17)\) and \(B=\operatorname{diag}(17,15)\).
Part (b): Prove that similarity preserves determinant and trace.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Both products equal \(\operatorname{diag}(255,255)\), so \([A,B]=AB-BA=0\).
Final answer: \([A,B]=0\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
For \(B=S^{-1}AS\),
\[\det B=\det(S^{-1})\det A\det S=\det A,\]
while cyclicity gives \(\operatorname{tr}B=\operatorname{tr}(ASS^{-1})=\operatorname{tr}A\).
Final answer: \(\det B=\det A\) and \(\operatorname{tr}B=\operatorname{tr}A\).
